caption:
The event is one thing. The story you narrate over it is another.

Save this, and rewrite one sentence you said to yourself today.

From "The Science of Learning Your Inner Speech." Link in bio.

#innerspeech #shakespeare #selftalk #mindset #perspective

text: “There is nothing either good or bad, but thinking makes it so.”
Hamlet says it to two old friends, in a prison of a castle.
The walls are the same for everyone. The *telling* is not.
Two people can live through the same afternoon.
One narrates it as a failure. One narrates it as a lesson.
The event did not change. The sentence did.
That sentence is usually inner speech.
Fast, familiar, and so close to you that it feels like fact.
Try catching the verdict inside the description.
*That meeting was a disaster.*
Strip it back: *The meeting ran long and I lost my place.*
Notice how much lighter the second version is.
It is just as honest. It simply leaves out the sentence.
You are not pretending things are good.
You are refusing to add a verdict you cannot prove.
What recent event are you calling bad because of the words you attached to it?
This is the thread behind the book *The Science of Learning Your Inner Speech*.
Learn to separate what happened from what you told yourself about it.
Hear the verdict.
*Edit the sentence.*

caption:
You can read everyone else and still be a stranger to yourself.

Send this to someone who thinks deeply.

From "Learn To Think For Yourself." Link in bio.

#selfawareness #laotzu #thinkforyourself #philosophy #mindset

text: “He who knows others is wise; he who knows himself is enlightened.”
Knowing others is a skill.
Knowing yourself is a *practice.*
We study people all day: their moods, their motives, their messages.
Rarely do we turn the same attention inward.
Self-knowledge is not a personality quiz.
It is noticing what you *do* when no one is watching.
What makes you defensive?
What do you avoid?
Those are not flaws. They are clues.
Thinking for yourself starts here.
You cannot trust your own judgment until you know what bends it.
Spend five minutes tonight.
Write down one reaction you had today, and *what it protected.*
What is one reaction of yours that you still do not fully understand?
This is the thread behind the book *Learn To Think For Yourself*.
Learn what shapes your thinking before you trust it.
Know the mind.
*Then lead it.*

caption:
Your mind is not broken. It is just never given a quiet room.

Try ten minutes of stillness tonight and save this as a reminder.

From "The 14-Day Clarity Reset." Link in bio.

#clarity #pascal #mindfulness #focus #mindset

text: “All the unhappiness of men arises from one single fact, that they cannot stay quietly in their own chamber.”
Pascal wrote this in the 1600s.
Imagine what he would say about the phone in your hand.
Stillness is uncomfortable because it leaves us alone with our thoughts.
So we reach for noise.
Noise is not rest.
It is a way of postponing the questions we have not answered.
Clarity does not arrive during the scroll.
It arrives in the gap *after* it.
Start small.
Ten minutes. No screen. One question on paper.
The room is not empty.
*You are in it.* That is the point.
When did you last sit for ten minutes with nothing to distract you?
This is the thread behind the book *The 14-Day Clarity Reset*.
Ten quiet minutes can reset a whole day.
Make space.
*Hear yourself.*

caption:
The words you use on yourself are the walls of the room you think in.

Save this and name one feeling precisely before bed.

From "The Science of Learning Your Inner Speech." Link in bio.

#innerspeech #wittgenstein #selftalk #language #mindset

text: “The limits of my language mean the limits of my world.”
If you have no word for a feeling, it is harder to see it.
If you have only a harsh word, it feels harsher.
Inner speech is the language you use on yourself.
Its vocabulary shapes what you can notice.
*I am a mess* is a small world.
*I am overwhelmed because I said yes to three things* is a larger one.
Precision is a kindness.
The more exactly you name it, the less it fills the whole sky.
Try a better word tonight.
Swap one blunt label for a more exact one.
A bigger vocabulary for your inner life
is a bigger room to think in.
What word could you use tonight for a feeling you have been calling something vague?
This is the thread behind the book *The Science of Learning Your Inner Speech*.
Widen the words, and the world widens too.
Find the word.
*Widen the world.*
